questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to study in the UK, so i took the chance when i was offered an exchange stay in Belfast.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy; the university offered a webinar in july, where i got all the information i needed. The university staff were very helpful whenever i had any questions, and replied quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I did not need any special assistance.
But if you need any assistance, they are quick to help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: For students who were on exchange for just one semester, we were offered to live in Elms Village BT9.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a shared kitchen with 8 electric cooking plates, 2 ovens, a microwave, long table, chairs, and a couch. Quite fine for 10 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for random fire alarms. There is one weekly test, however, the fire alarm went of at strange times, sometimes during the middle of the night/early morning. 
The heating didn't work many times, and the isolation wasn't very good.
There's also a shared bathroom and shower. 

Overall, it's fine for one semester. I had a good experience in the accommodation, despite the problems above.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There were not that many courses to choose between. We found out after we arrived, which courses we had to change. This was stressful, since we had to do this while finding everything else out. 
However, we had a window of two-three weeks where we could switch courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to contact the staff. They were always very helpful and always replied quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of the three courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to the possibility of having to change most of the courses you selected. Add more courses to your learning agreement, so that you won't have to stress about it while you're there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes i took were all for last-year undergraduate students in law.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The courses are very descriptive, and have you deal with theory and ideas around the law, rather than problem cases. 
There are very few classes, and you have to study a lot yourself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contract Law, International Trade Law, and Law and Technology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed Contract Law, since that course dealt more with the application of the law in problem cases, rather than just theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The apartments and kitchen were almost completely empty, when we arrived.
So i had to buy a duvet and pillow, and a lot of pans, pots, cultery, etc. in the first few days.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: They were less expensive than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different clubs, events, and associations available to the students. The university has a sports centre with a gym. If you're on exchange, you get a free off-peak membership.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The clubs are a great way to meet different people. I would recommend the sailing club, because of it's social events. I also joined the archery and snooker club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The giant's causeway and Titanic museum are a must. The city centre is very charming, with a lot of pubs, cafes and restaurants. Belfast has a lot of history and culture to explore, like f.eks. the peace walls, different museums, and so on. I would recommend visiting nearby towns, like Londonderry/Derry for the history and culture. 
You can take a 2-hour bus to Dublin, which is a nice trip. It's also easy and cheap to fly to other cities in the UK mainland, so i would also recommend going there for a weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
For me, it was very easy to adjust. You share a floor with other exchange students, so everyone is in the same boat. 
The locals are very friendly and helpful, and it's very easy to get to know them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be very open and curious. Don't be afraid of not being too good at english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The accent was a bit difficult in the beginning, but i got used to it very fast.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and politeness of the locals. They are also very open and talkative, so it was easy to become friends with them. It's not for everyone, but i really enjoyed the humour/banter over there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Rain clothes and an umbrella - the weather is bad. 
2) Public transport isn't the best - just be ready for it.
3) Do as much as you can in regards to trips, experiences, events, meeting new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are no direct flights to Belfast from Copenhagen. Fly to Dublin and take the express bus from the airport to Belfast. I flew transit and had too many problems with it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Coming in contact with different people, cultures, ways of living and thinking, etc. 
The experience really broadened my horizon and understanding of people and the world. 
I am also now friends with people from different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a different way of school and teaching. I am very used to the way things are done in UPCH, and navigating a completely different schoolsystem was really stressing and rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
